title: Afterimage (Not on This Page)
summary: A flag painted in the wrong colours fatigues your retina, then a blank field lets your own eye render the real Stars and Stripes — an artwork with no pixels.
mechanism: Timed two-state surface: 20s fixation on a complementary-colour SVG flag, then a crossfade to a neutral field where the opponent-process afterimage forms in the viewer's eye, not on screen.
references: Ewald Hering, opponent-process theory of colour vision
